newsitem.title: USA: River restrictions eased at New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: River restrictions eased at New Orleans.

text.p: Maritime traffic moved closer to normal on the Mississippi River Tuesday following a dramatic weekend accident in which a crippled freighter ploughed into a New Orleans wharf near the city's French Quarter.
Coast Guard officials said the Mississippi River near New Orleans was opened to a depth of 40 feet on Tuesday afternoon. Under normal conditions, drafts of up to 45 feet are allowed.
"It is at 40 feet at the present time, both ways," said Coast Guard petty officer Raymond Crooks at New Orleans.
Shipping at the Port of New Orleans has been sharply curtailed since Saturday, when the grain freighter, the Bright Field, lost power and slammed into a dockside shopping centre.
The 735-foot Liberian-flagged freighter damaged the Riverwalk shopping mall, a wing of the New Orleans Hilton Hotel and a parking garage when it slammed into the wharf.
The Coast Guard has gradually scaled back the draft restrictions on the river that were imposed over the weekend, raising the limit to 35 feet by late Monday.
Officials said port operations would not return to normal until at least the end of the week.
"We're estimating traffic will be back to normal by the end of the week," Crooks said. "It could be next week too," he added.

Traffic was currently limited to one-way at a time, Crooks said, in order to maintain a quarter-mile distance from the wreckage. Coast Guard officials have expressed concern that the passage of larger vessels could further damage the wharf or make salvage operations more difficult.

Ship operators continued to experience delays near the port, but officials said the congestion had eased somewhat. Two or three outbound ships were backed up waiting to exit the port Tuesday afternoon.
Officials have yet to determine how they would remove the wreckage, but an announcement on salvage operations may be forthcoming later Tuesday, Crooks said.
